plain.text: As the number of disciples grew, the Greek-speaking Jewish believers complained that their widows were being overlooked in the daily food distribution. The twelve gathered everyone and said they should not neglect the ministry of God's word to wait on tables. They asked the believers to choose seven men known to be full of the Spirit and wisdom to take on this task. Everyone agreed. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit, and six others. The apostles prayed and laid their hands on them. The word of God spread, and the number of disciples in Jerusalem increased rapidly; even many priests became obedient to the faith.

Stephen, full of God's grace and power, performed great wonders and signs. Some members of a synagogue began to argue with him, but they could not stand up against his wisdom or the Spirit by whom he spoke. So they secretly persuaded men to say, "We have heard Stephen speak words of blasphemy against Moses and against God." They stirred up the people and leaders, seized Stephen and brought him before the council. False witnesses said he spoke against the temple and the law. All who were sitting in the council looked at him and saw that his face was like the face of an angel.

summary.bigIdea: The church solves a fairness problem by sharing leadership, and Stephen, full of the Spirit, faces false accusations.
points: Widows are being overlooked, so seven Spirit-filled men are chosen to serve.
The word of God keeps spreading.
Stephen is arrested on false charges, yet his face shines like an angel's.
summary.reflection: The church listened to a complaint and fixed it fairly. Is there someone overlooked whom you could help?
